Minnesota Golden Gophers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy. The guide records Minnesota ranking 116th nationally on the ground at 3.57 yards per carry and 127th in total offense, and places the burden on the offensive line.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide credits redshirt sophomore Drake Lindsey with starting all 13 games as a freshman for 2,432 yards and a 19-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio, calls him a potential special player, and makes his progress conditional on the offensive line.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 43) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 13 returning starters — totalling 17, among the highest in the guide.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Perry Thompson from Auburn, Bennett Warren from Tennessee, TJ Bush from Cal by way of Liberty, and Naquan Crowder, Sid Kaba and Xion Chapman from Marshall and FIU.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.portal_recruiting: Addressed as retention as much as acquisition — the guide notes running back Darius Taylor turned down portal interest to stay, and records the loss of Koi Perich to Oregon as stinging more than a typical portal exit.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.vsin_assessment: Steady, with the ceiling as the open question. The guide records P.J. Fleck entering a tenth season with bowls in seven of nine years, a 7-0 bowl record and eight or more wins in four of the last five, then frames its question as whether a steady programme can occasionally challenge the conference elite.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.strengths: A decade of head-coaching continuity with both coordinators and the quarterback also returning, a Stability Score of 17, 68% of 2025 production back per ESPN's Bill Connelly, and a Big Ten-leading pass rusher in Anthony Smith with 12.5 sacks.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.concerns: No true No. 1 receiver, doubts on the interior of both lines, the loss of Koi Perich which the guide says may lower the defense's ceiling, and the loss of the top four defensive tackles into a conference the guide notes contains several of the country's top-10 offensive lines.
Minnesota Golden Gophers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Nebraska Cornhuskers.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Matt Rhule arriving in 2023 known for quick rebuilds at Temple and Baylor, and notes that three years on he is 19-19.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.dc: Rob Aurich, in from a top-10 San Diego State defense, replacing the dismissed John Butler.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.dc_status: New — the guide records John Butler's dismissal and Aurich's hiring, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The offense is identified as Dana Holgorsen's Air Raid.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide refers to Dana Holgorsen's Air Raid, and notes TJ Lateef already knows it.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.defensive_scheme: Named, and changing. The guide describes a transition from 3-3-5 to Rob Aurich's 4-2-5 scheme.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated philosophy beyond the Air Raid label.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.personnel: Addressed only through the 3-3-5 to 4-2-5 defensive change.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record, and the guide records a development that went the other way: Dylan Raiola, a legacy recruit expected to be the answer, went 13-9 as a starter over two seasons before breaking his leg against USC after a 6-2 start and transferring to Oregon.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinator and quarterback both change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 3 for 15 returning starters, totalling 10.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.staff_turnover: Substantial on defense and on the offensive line. The guide records defensive coordinator John Butler and defensive line coach Terry Bradden dismissed, and offensive line coach Donovan Raiola — Dylan Raiola's uncle — fired.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.prior_school: San Diego State for Aurich, and the connection extends to the roster: linebacker Owen Chambliss follows him from San Diego State. Other additions the guide records are Anthony Colandrea from UNLV, Kwazi Gilmer from UCLA, Paul Mubenga from LSU, Brendan Black from Iowa State, Tree Babalade from South Carolina, Owen Stoudmire from Boston College, Jahsear Whittington from Pitt, Anthony Jones Jr from UCLA and Dexter Foster from Oregon State.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.portal_recruiting: Heavily used on both lines and at quarterback, and pointedly not used at running back: the guide records Nebraska choosing not to replace first-team All-American Emmett Johnson from the portal, turning instead to sophomores Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.vsin_assessment: Hot seat, stated repeatedly. The guide says the natives are getting restless at 19-19, notes Anthony Colandrea must meet high expectations to cool Rhule's seat, and concludes that with a new defensive scheme and a difficult schedule Nebraska looks middling again and Rhule's seat will only get hotter.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.strengths: A head coach with a documented record of quick rebuilds at Temple and Baylor, offensive-coordinator continuity in a known system, a Mountain West Player of the Year at quarterback, a rebuilt and more agile offensive line, a secondary with three starters back, and a defensive coordinator in from a top-10 unit.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.concerns: A .500 record over three seasons, the loss of a legacy quarterback to the portal, a wholesale scheme change from 3-3-5 to 4-2-5, a defense that conceded 131 points across its final three games and ranked 98th against the run with 22 sacks in 13 games, and an unreplaced 1,451-yard rusher.
Nebraska Cornhuskers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked conclusion is directional rather than priced: Nebraska looks middling again and the seat gets hotter.

Northwestern Wildcats.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed as head-coaching experience beyond Northwestern. The guide records David Braun's background as extensively FCS, at Northern Iowa and North Dakota State, and notes he was 2023 Big Ten Coach of the Year.
Northwestern Wildcats.oc: Chip Kelly, with Jerry Neuheisel as quarterbacks coach.
Northwestern Wildcats.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide records Kelly's arrival as finally giving Northwestern a creative offensive mind.
Northwestern Wildcats.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Northwestern Wildcats.play_caller: Chip Kelly, as the new coordinator.
Northwestern Wildcats.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide describes a fast no-huddle spread and says Aidan Chiles is the athletic, mobile quarterback Kelly wants in it.
Northwestern Wildcats.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Northwestern Wildcats.tempo: Stated as fast — the guide describes Kelly's offense as a fast no-huddle spread.
Northwestern Wildcats.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide identifies a three-pronged run game with Caleb Komolafe, gadget back Joseph Hinton and Gavin Sawchuk as one route to rebuilding the quarterback.
Northwestern Wildcats.qb_development: Framed as an explicit coaching assignment. The guide asks whether Kelly can rebuild Chiles — benched after nine games at Michigan State and 8-12 as a starter across two seasons — sees the scheme fit, and insists Kelly must also restore his confidence. It notes quarterbacks coach Jerry Neuheisel recruited Chiles out of high school.
Northwestern Wildcats.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback both change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 9.
Northwestern Wildcats.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive side, where Kelly and Neuheisel arrive.
Northwestern Wildcats.prior_school: Michigan State, twice over — the guide notes the symmetry that Michigan State has Northwestern's old coach in Pat Fitzgerald and Northwestern has Michigan State's old quarterback in Aidan Chiles, and that the two meet on 17 October. Other additions recorded are Gavin Sawchuk from Florida State, Grant Seagren from Oklahoma State and Jamaal Johnson from UCF.
Northwestern Wildcats.portal_recruiting: Tied to the coaching problem the guide sets out: Braun will have to coach up players from Group of Six, FCS and Division II programmes who are in line to start.
Northwestern Wildcats.vsin_assessment: Credit for what Braun has managed, with the talent gap stated plainly. The guide records him doing more with less as 2023 Big Ten Coach of the Year while navigating the fallout from Fitzgerald's termination, and marks the Fitzgerald chapter as finally closed following the settled lawsuit and his return to coaching at Michigan State. Its concrete caveat is that Braun must coach up lower-division starters, and its closing judgement is that the defense can only carry the team so far against this schedule.
Northwestern Wildcats.strengths: A head coach the guide credits with doing more with less, a coordinator hire it calls a creative offensive mind with a scheme that fits the incoming quarterback, five of the top six pass catchers returning, a settled offensive line, and a secondary the guide calls the team's best unit.
Northwestern Wildcats.concerns: Aidan Chiles' accuracy and ball security potentially reappearing, a pass rush that ranked 14th in the Big Ten with 23 sacks and lost nearly half of them, and a starting lineup drawing on Group of Six, FCS and Division II talent.
Northwestern Wildcats.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Ohio State Buckeyes.dc: Matt Patricia, an NFL hire, entering his second season.
Ohio State Buckeyes.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Ohio State Buckeyes.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Ohio State Buckeyes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide attributes the expected tactical change to Arthur Smith.
Ohio State Buckeyes.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide states the direction of travel instead: Arthur Smith wants to run more aggressively and will let Julian Sayin use his legs.
Ohio State Buckeyes.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Patricia producing the country's No. 1 defense at 9.3 points and 219.1 yards allowed per game in his first year while replacing eight starters.
Ohio State Buckeyes.tempo: Stated and expected to change. The guide records that Ohio State ran the slowest-paced offense in college football, asks whether the tempo was too slow and answers yes, and expects the training wheels to come off Sayin.
Ohio State Buckeyes.run_pass: Addressed as a stated intention: while the downfield passing game will be the most explosive element, Arthur Smith wants to run more aggressively.
Ohio State Buckeyes.qb_development: Addressed as an expectation of released constraint rather than a coaching record: the guide expects the training wheels to come off Sayin and suggests Arthur Smith could do for the offense what Patricia did for the defense.
Ohio State Buckeyes.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 43) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 14 returning starters — totalling 17, among the highest in the guide.
Ohio State Buckeyes.staff_turnover: None recorded. The guide's staff observation is about method: having succeeded with an NFL hire in Matt Patricia, Ryan Day repeated the approach on offense with Arthur Smith.
Ohio State Buckeyes.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records James Smith from Alabama, John Walker from UCF, Earl Little Jr from Florida State, Terry Moore from Duke and Devin McCuin from UTSA.
Ohio State Buckeyes.portal_recruiting: Aggressive despite the results. The guide notes Ohio State has not stood pat: 18 portal additions, 50 new players and another top-five recruiting class.
Ohio State Buckeyes.vsin_assessment: Self-critical on the coach's behalf. The guide entertains whether Day became too conservative and whether the tempo was too slow, answers yes to both, then concludes the clearest reason for the two losses is that the line was beaten up front. It credits the NFL hiring method through Patricia's No. 1 defense.
Ohio State Buckeyes.strengths: A Stability Score of 17 with both NFL-hire coordinators retained, arguably the best quarterback-receiver combination in the country, a coordinator who produced the No. 1 defense while replacing eight starters, four returning offensive line starters, and continuing top-five recruiting.
Ohio State Buckeyes.concerns: Replacing eight more drafted defensive starters with no superstar equivalent to last year's, an offensive line that conceded five sacks against Indiana and five more against Miami after allowing six all regular season, and finding a second receiving option behind Jeremiah Smith.
Ohio State Buckeyes.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Oregon Ducks.oc: Drew Mehringer, promoted internally after Will Stein left for Kentucky.
Oregon Ducks.dc: Chris Hampton, promoted internally after Tosh Lupoi left for Cal. The guide records that Dan Lanning calls the defense himself.
Oregon Ducks.oc_status: New — the guide records Will Stein leaving for a head coaching job and Mehringer being promoted, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Oregon Ducks.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Oregon Ducks.play_caller: Dan Lanning on defense, explicitly — the guide states he calls it himself and on that basis expects another elite unit.
Oregon Ducks.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Oregon Ducks.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Oregon Ducks.qb_development: Not addressed as a coaching record. The guide records Dante Moore turning down the NFL Draft after 3,565 yards and 30 touchdowns in his first year starting and calls him justifiably a Heisman favorite, while keeping the big-stage question open.
Oregon Ducks.continuity: Head coach, defensive coordinator and quarterback return; the offensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 4, plus 3 for 15 returning starters, totalling 14.
Oregon Ducks.staff_turnover: Framed as a consequence of success. The guide says Oregon starts as a victim of its own success, losing offensive coordinator Will Stein to Kentucky and Tosh Lupoi to Cal, both for head coaching jobs, with Drew Mehringer and Chris Hampton promoted internally.
Oregon Ducks.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff, which was promoted from within. On the roster the guide records D'Antre Robinson from North Carolina and Jerome Simmons from Louisiana-Monroe.
Oregon Ducks.portal_recruiting: Addressed mainly as retention and as targeted defensive line depth. The guide records 66% of net production returning per ESPN's Bill Connelly despite the staff churn.
Oregon Ducks.vsin_assessment: Strong, with a specific and repeated postseason reservation. The guide records Lanning at 48-8 since 2022 with playoff appearances in both years and a run through the Big Ten in Oregon's first conference season, and expects another elite defense because he calls it himself. Against that it poses a genuine puzzle it does not resolve: this is the only offensive line to be a Joe Moore Award finalist in each of the last three years, so why does it struggle in big games — 11 three-and-outs, 11 sacks allowed and 21 tackles for loss across the last two playoff exits.
Oregon Ducks.strengths: A 48-8 head-coaching record with a defense he calls himself, eight returning defensive starters, a Heisman-favorite quarterback who turned down the draft, possibly the country's best defensive line, and internal promotions that preserved continuity through two coordinator departures.
Oregon Ducks.concerns: Losing both coordinators to head-coaching jobs in one offseason, three offensive line starters to replace on a unit the guide says struggles in big games, a defense that ranked 52nd nationally in third-down stops, and young skill players who must step up from backup roles.
Oregon Ducks.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Penn State Nittany Lions.previous_hc_experience: Extensive and central to the guide's assessment. The Coaching Carousel records a four-year run at Toledo it calls great and a decade at Iowa State it calls tremendous, built up amid a lot of financial and reputational shortcomings in a high-octane offensive conference. The team pages record the eight-year, $70.5 million contract and note Penn State missed on Kalani Sitake first.
Penn State Nittany Lions.oc: Taylor Mouser, brought from Iowa State among 11 assistants.
Penn State Nittany Lions.dc: D'Anton Lynn, a Texas native and former Penn State player, hired immediately after improving USC's defense over two years.
Penn State Nittany Lions.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Penn State Nittany Lions.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Penn State Nittany Lions.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Penn State Nittany Lions.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Penn State Nittany Lions.defensive_scheme: Named. The guide describes a 4-2-5 alignment that is new to these players, with the mitigating factor that seven of Lynn's defensive starters also started for an Iowa State group that finished one place outside the top 25 in scoring defense at 20.2 points allowed.
Penn State Nittany Lions.personnel: Addressed only through the 4-2-5 defensive alignment.
Penn State Nittany Lions.qb_development: Not addressed as a development record. The guide's quarterback concern is availability rather than coaching: Rocco Becht made 39 consecutive starts at Iowa State despite a torn labrum, a sprained AC joint and two concussions last season, then had offseason surgery limiting him to 7-on-7 work.
Penn State Nittany Lions.continuity: Broken everywhere. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 3 for 16 returning starters, totalling 3 — the lowest kind of score the table produces.
Penn State Nittany Lions.staff_turnover: Complete, and replaced en bloc. Campbell brought 11 assistants including coordinator Taylor Mouser from Ames. The guide records that James Franklin was sacked the day after a home loss as a three-touchdown favorite to Northwestern, that the team rallied to win its last four under interim coach Terry Smith, and that Smith stays on as associate head coach.
Penn State Nittany Lions.prior_school: Iowa State, overwhelmingly — 11 assistants, coordinator Taylor Mouser, quarterback Rocco Becht, backup Alex Manske, running back Carson Hansen, and his top four pass catchers Ben Brahmer, Gabe Burkle, Chase Sowell and Brett Eskildsen, within 24 players in total. D'Anton Lynn comes from USC, and the guide notes he is a former Penn State player.
Penn State Nittany Lions.portal_recruiting: Explicitly modelled on another programme. Campbell brought 24 Iowa State players within 40 total transfers as Penn State replaces 70 players including eight drafted last spring; the guide reads this as an attempt to duplicate Curt Cignetti's Indiana blueprint and draws the comparison in figures — Cignetti brought 29 transfers to Indiana in 2024, 12 from James Madison and 22 from the Group of Five or lower, while 36 of Campbell's 40 are from Power Four schools. The Coaching Carousel adds that Campbell has strong Ohio ties which should help with recruiting, and that hiring Lynn gives Penn State connections from coast to coast.
Penn State Nittany Lions.vsin_assessment: The hardest hire in the guide to project, by its own statement. The Coaching Carousel says of all the Power Four hires this is the hardest one to project, credits Toledo and Iowa State, then states plainly that Penn State is a different beast and this is a BIG job. Its stated question is what Campbell can do with more talent, having maximized what he could recruit at Iowa State — and it says that question may not be answered in 2026. The team pages expect the Iowa State transfers to band together as the James Madison group did at Indiana and set a new culture, while acknowledging the step up in competition.
Penn State Nittany Lions.strengths: A decade-long record of building a programme with fewer resources, a coordinator staff transplanted intact from Ames, a defensive coordinator with a documented USC improvement and seven of his own former starters in the scheme, 16 returning starters, and recruiting ties spanning Ohio and Texas.
Penn State Nittany Lions.concerns: A Stability Score of 3 with every continuity component at zero, a quarterback coming off surgery behind a room whose only other experienced arm is a Division III transfer, and the guide's own doubt about whether the step up from the Big 12 to the Big Ten is absorbed in year one.
Penn State Nittany Lions.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
Penn State Nittany Lions.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens by saying that of all the Power Four hires, this is the hardest one to project in his estimation. He credits the record — a four-year run at Toledo he calls great and a decade in Ames he calls tremendous, built up amid a lot of financial and reputational shortcomings in a high-octane offensive conference — then sets the scale against it: Penn State is a different beast, and this is a BIG job. He identifies two assets: Campbell's strong Ohio ties, which should help with recruiting, and the hire of D'Anton Lynn, a Texas native, as defensive coordinator, giving Penn State connections from coast to coast. His closing frame is what stood out at Iowa State — how Campbell maximized the talent he was able to recruit — and the question that follows: with more fertile recruiting grounds, what can he do with more talent? He answers that this will be the big question, and maybe one not quite answered in 2026.
